analysis.title: EcoFlash: European resilience, American vigour
key_insights: Eurozone Q3 GDP grew 0.4% q/q in the Eurostat preliminary flash estimate, above consensus and BNP's Nowcast of 0.3%. Ireland contributed 0.2 pp, so growth excluding Ireland was 0.2% q/q, in line with the 0.2-0.3% q/q recent average.

BNP forecasts 1.1% Eurozone growth for 2026 and sees upside risk. The 2026 growth carry-over stands at 1.0%, and the European Commission's October surveys show a further improvement in industrial activity expectations.
Country contributions to Eurozone Q3 q/q GDP: Spain +0.07 pp, Germany +0.06 pp, Netherlands +0.04 pp, France -0.03 pp, Italy zero.
Germany's real GDP grew 0.2% q/q in Q3 after 0.3% in Q2, the fourth consecutive quarter of growth. Consumption rose slightly, investment edged down and export momentum slowed markedly versus Q2.
Italy's GDP stagnated in Q3 against a 0.1% consensus. Industry value added fell, offset by services and agriculture. Domestic demand's positive contribution was cancelled by negative net trade.

Spain's GDP grew 0.6% q/q in Q3 (0.7% in Q2), in line with expectations. Domestic demand contributed 0.5 pp and net exports 0.1 pp. Private consumption rose 0.6%, public consumption 0.9% and investment 0.7%. Exports grew 1.3% and imports 1.1%.

France's GDP fell 0.1% q/q in Q3 (stagnation in Q2), against a +0.1% consensus. Output of other transport equipment, which includes aerospace, dropped 4.5% q/q, goods production fell 1.2%, exports fell 1.7% and business investment fell 0.4%. Net trade subtracted 0.6 pp.
French household consumption rose 0.4% q/q, helped by electric vehicle purchases (registrations up 112% y/y in Q3). Public consumption rose 0.3% and market services activity rose 0.3%.

Airbus has confirmed its delivery targets for the year, with engine supply problems expected to be resolved. BNP forecasts French Q4 growth of 0.3% q/q, and annual growth of 0.3% in 2026 and 0.8% in 2027.
US Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualised (0.8% q/q) versus 2.2% (0.6% q/q) in Q2, the fastest pace since Q3 2025. BNP says activity is almost immune to the energy shock.

US private non-residential investment grew 12.7% annualised, unmatched since the post-Covid reopening. AI-related components grew 18.5% annualised, and other investment rose 3.8% annualised for a second straight quarter after contracting throughout 2025.

US real household consumption grew 2.5% annualised while the saving rate fell to 3.8% from 4.4% in the previous quarter. Imports surged 19.7% annualised, led by AI-related IT, semiconductor and telecom imports (103.8% annualised), so net trade weighed on GDP.
earnings_insights: Airbus has confirmed its delivery targets for the year despite a sharp Q3 drop in French aerospace output, with engine supply problems expected to be resolved.

BNP's forecast, with upside risk because the carry-over is already 1.0%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fastest pace since Q3 2025, driven by private domestic demand, led by AI-related investment.
Strongest since the post-Covid reopening. AI-related components grew 18.5% and other investment 3.8%.

risk_factors: Irish GDP figures are volatile and contributed 0.2 pp to the Eurozone Q3 print.
Export momentum in Germany slowed markedly versus Q2.
Industrial weakness in Italy and French aerospace supply disruptions weighed on Q3 output.
US consumption growth relies on a falling saving rate, now at 3.8%.
US net trade is weighed down by a surge in AI-related imports.
The current energy shock is a drag on Eurozone growth.
geopolitical: The report refers to a current energy shock, which US activity has largely shrugged off.
